title: Preventing Dehydration
learning_objective: Stay hydrated, replace fluids, and seek medical advice for dehydration signs.

sections.heading: Core concepts
sections.content: Dehydration occurs when you lose more water than you take in. Common causes include not drinking enough water, hot weather, exercise, fever, vomiting, or diarrhea. Signs include thirst, dry mouth, dark urine, and dizziness. Prevent dehydration by drinking water regularly, especially during hot weather and exercise. Seek medical advice if signs of dehydration are severe or persistent.

sections.heading: Practical guidance
sections.content: Drink water regularly, especially before, during, and after exercise. Replace fluids lost through sweating, vomiting, or diarrhea. Avoid alcohol and caffeine as they can dehydrate you. Stay hydrated by eating fruits and vegetables that are high in water content.

sections.heading: What to observe or ask
sections.content: If you have a persistent fever, monitor your temperature, rest, and maintain fluids. If signs of dehydration are severe or persistent, seek advice from a healthcare professional. sections.heading: When to seek help
sections.content: Severe dehydration signs include severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, signs of stroke, severe bleeding, loss of consciousness, or a severe allergic reaction. Seek emergency care for these signs.

title: Understanding Persistent Fever
learning_objective: Persistent fever can be a sign of illness. It's important to monitor your temperature, rest, and stay hydrated. Seek medical advice if the fever persists or is accompanied by concerning symptoms.

sections.heading: Core concepts
sections.content: A persistent fever is a high body temperature that doesn't go down. It can be caused by infections, inflammation, or other health issues. Dehydration and lack of rest can also cause a fever.

sections.heading: Practical guidance
sections.content: If you have a persistent fever, monitor your temperature, rest, and drink plenty of fluids. If the fever is severe or accompanied by other concerning symptoms, seek medical advice.

sections.heading: What to observe or ask
sections.content: If you have a persistent fever, it's important to observe your symptoms and ask your healthcare provider about them. This can help in diagnosing the cause of the fever and receiving appropriate treatment.

sections.heading: When to seek help
sections.content: If you have a persistent fever, it's important to seek medical advice if the fever is severe, accompanied by other concerning symptoms, or if you have a history of chronic health conditions.

title: Reducing Respiratory Infection Spread
learning_objective: Learn effective strategies to prevent and manage respiratory infections.

sections.heading: Core concepts
sections.content: Respiratory infections can be spread through coughing, sneezing, and close contact. Covering your mouth and nose when you cough or sneeze, washing hands frequently, and staying home when you're sick are crucial steps to reduce the spread of infections.

sections.heading: Practical guidance
sections.content: Use a tissue or flexed elbow to cover your mouth and nose when you cough or sneeze. Wash your hands frequently with soap and water for at least 20 seconds, or use an alcohol-based hand sanitizer. Avoid touching your eyes, nose, and mouth. Clean and disinfect frequently touched surfaces.

sections.heading: What to observe or ask
sections.content: If you have a persistent fever, monitor your temperature and rest. If your fever persists or is severe, seek advice from a healthcare professional. If you have symptoms of a respiratory infection, such as a sore throat, cough, or difficulty breathing, seek medical attention promptly.

sections.heading: When to seek help
sections.content: If you experience severe breathing difficulties, chest pain, signs of a stroke, severe bleeding, loss of consciousness, or a severe allergic reaction, seek emergency care immediately. For other symptoms, consult a healthcare professional if they persist or worsen.

title: The Importance of Sleep for Whole-Health
learning_objective: Sleep is crucial for physical recovery, mental health, and overall well-being. It supports immune function and mood regulation.

sections.heading: Core concepts
sections.content: Sleep is essential for physical recovery, mood regulation, and immune function. It helps in memory consolidation and emotional processing. Adequate sleep is vital for overall health and longevity.

sections.heading: Practical guidance
sections.content: Establish a consistent sleep schedule, create a relaxing bedtime routine, and avoid stimulating activities close to bedtime. Use the bedroom for sleep only. Consider using a sleep mask and earplugs if needed. Maintain a cool, dark, and quiet environment. Limit caffeine and alcohol intake before bedtime. Exercise regularly but avoid vigorous activities close to bedtime.

sections.heading: What to observe or ask
sections.content: If you frequently feel tired, struggle with concentration, or have mood swings, consider your sleep habits. Ask your healthcare provider about potential sleep disorders or sleep apnea. If you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, discuss strategies to improve your sleep quality.

sections.heading: When to seek help
sections.content: If you experience persistent sleep problems, severe sleep deprivation, or signs of sleep disorders, such as daytime sleepiness, frequent awakenings, or difficulty falling asleep, it's important to seek help from a healthcare professional. They can provide appropriate assessments and treatments.

title: Recognising Urgent Warning Signs
learning_objective: Recognising urgent warning signs is crucial for timely medical intervention. Knowing what to look for can save lives.

sections.heading: Core concepts
sections.content: Urgent warning signs include severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, signs of stroke, severe bleeding, loss of consciousness, and severe allergic reactions. These symptoms require immediate medical attention.

sections.heading: Practical guidance
sections.content: If you notice any of these signs, seek emergency care immediately. Do not delay. Time is critical in managing these conditions.

sections.heading: What to observe or ask
sections.content: Look for signs of distress, such as difficulty breathing, severe pain, or unresponsiveness. Ask for medical help if you are unsure about the severity of the symptoms.

sections.heading: When to seek help
sections.content: Seek emergency care for severe or life-threatening symptoms. Do not delay, as prompt medical intervention can significantly improve outcomes.

title: Preventive Measures for Everyday Health
learning_objective: Maintain good health through daily habits.

sections.heading: Core concepts
sections.content: Preventive measures include hydration, fever management, respiratory infection prevention, sleep quality, and recognizing urgent medical needs.

sections.heading: Practical guidance
sections.content: Drink water regularly, rest, and maintain fluids. Monitor fever, cover coughs, and stay home when sick. Ensure adequate sleep and discuss sleep issues with healthcare professionals.

sections.heading: What to observe or ask
sections.content: Seek medical advice for significant dehydration, persistent fever, respiratory infections, sleep problems, and severe symptoms.

sections.heading: When to seek help
sections.content: Urgent medical attention is needed for severe breathing difficulties, chest pain, signs of stroke, severe bleeding, loss of consciousness, or severe allergic reactions.

key_takeaways: Stay hydrated, manage fever, prevent infections, ensure adequate sleep, and seek medical help for severe symptoms.

title: Tracking Symptoms Responsibly
learning_objective: Learn how to manage symptoms effectively and seek help when necessary.

sections.heading: Core concepts
sections.content: Symptoms are your body's way of telling you something is wrong. Tracking them responsibly helps you understand your health better and when to seek medical advice.

sections.heading: Practical guidance
sections.content: Keep a symptom diary. Note down the symptoms, their duration, and how they affect your daily life. This helps you and your healthcare provider track your health.

sections.heading: What to observe or ask
sections.content: If you notice a symptom that worries you, or if it persists, ask your healthcare provider about it. Don't hesitate to seek help if you're unsure.

sections.heading: When to seek help
sections.content: Seek medical advice if you experience severe symptoms like chest pain, difficulty breathing, severe bleeding, or signs of a stroke. These are emergencies that require urgent care.

title: When to Seek Professional Advice
learning_objective: When to seek professional advice is crucial for maintaining health and preventing complications. Seek medical advice for persistent fever, severe respiratory infections, severe bleeding, loss of consciousness, or signs of stroke.

sections.heading: Core concepts
sections.content: Seek medical advice for persistent fever, severe respiratory infections, severe bleeding, loss of consciousness, or signs of stroke.

sections.heading: Practical guidance

sections.heading: What to observe or ask
sections.content: Observe signs of dehydration, persistent fever, severe respiratory infections, severe bleeding, loss of consciousness, or signs of stroke. Ask about your symptoms and treatment options.

sections.heading: When to seek help

title: Health Information Literacy
learning_objective: Learn to critically evaluate health information and make informed decisions.

sections.heading: Core concepts
sections.content: Health information literacy involves understanding the quality of health information, recognizing misinformation, and critically evaluating sources. It empowers individuals to make informed decisions about their health.

sections.heading: Practical guidance
sections.content: Seek reliable sources of health information, such as reputable medical journals, government health websites, and certified health professionals. Use evidence-based practices and avoid unproven remedies. Stay informed about new research and guidelines.

sections.heading: What to observe or ask
sections.content: Be aware of warning signs of health issues, such as persistent fever, severe pain, or unexplained symptoms. Consider asking your healthcare provider about your health concerns and treatment options.

sections.heading: When to seek help
sections.content: Seek medical advice for persistent symptoms, severe pain, signs of infection, or concerning health issues. Do not hesitate to contact a healthcare professional if you feel unwell or have concerns about your health.

title: Building a Practical Personal Wellness Plan
learning_objective: Develop a personalized wellness plan to improve overall health and well-being.

sections.heading: Core concepts
sections.content: A wellness plan includes regular physical activity, balanced nutrition, adequate sleep, stress management, and regular medical check-ups. These practices help prevent illness and promote longevity.

sections.heading: Practical guidance
sections.content: Start by setting realistic goals, tracking progress, and adjusting as needed. Consult with a healthcare provider to tailor the plan to your specific health needs.

sections.heading: What to observe or ask
sections.content: Keep track of your symptoms, monitor your health, and ask questions if you're unsure about your diet, exercise, or sleep habits. Consult a healthcare professional for personalized advice.

sections.heading: When to seek help
sections.content: Seek medical attention if you experience severe symptoms such as persistent high fever, severe pain, difficulty breathing, or unexplained weight loss. Always prioritize your health and safety.

key_takeaways: Seek medical attention for severe symptoms
